1#main: Prohibition of wearing shoes for a mourner. And it contains 5 seifim. A mourner is forbidden to wear shoes — specifically of leather; but a shoe of cloth, reed, hair, or wood is permitted, for a shoe is only of leather; and if of wood covered with leather — forbidden.
2#main: A woman is permitted to wear shoes all thirty days because cold is hard for her.
3#main: Everyone is permitted to wear shoes in a place where there is danger of scorpion.
4#main: A mourner and excommunicated person who were traveling on the road are permitted to wear shoes; and when they reach the city they remove them; and some say if it is a city mostly gentiles they do not remove until they enter the Jewish street.
5#main: If one must remove a shoe in the cemetery after the deceased is buried — it was explained in siman 375: {Rama: Some say he must walk barefoot from the cemetery to his house if his father or mother died (Kol Bo in the name of R' Yehudah); and I have not seen people practice thus.}
